target_customer: Grocery shoppers via retailers such as Whole Foods; earlier office workers at WeWork
problem: Healthy prepared food is hard to deliver fresh at scale and wasteful.
business_model: Wholesale of fresh prepared food to grocers with in-house production and cold chain

technical_complexity.rationale: Food production and cold chain operations with inventory forecasting; operationally hard but not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Cold chain logistics and retailer relationships are slow to build but product is copyable.

market_need_then: Founders sold meals from coolers at LA WeWorks in 2018 and said they built a cult following with affordable healthy meals (TechCrunch 2022).

identity.logo: Logo file described only as logo-dark

branding.community_and_virality: Cult following at WeWork per company; Glendale cafe opened after a decade on shelves

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly name with grassroots following but a generic word and a .co domain; no brand press beyond company statements.

pivots.from: Selling meals from coolers to WeWork offices
pivots.to: Wholesale to coffee shops then grocery stores
pivots.why: Per TechCrunch and company site; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Positive Food Co. grew from selling out of coolers at LA WeWorks to Whole Foods and Bristol Farms, 86 to 88 California stores in 2022, with in-house production and a point of sale driven inventory model. It raised a reported $7M in August 2022 and is active with 47 staff; a Glendale cafe is planned.
notes: TechCrunch does not state a round label; aggregators call it Series U or seed or Series A, so stage is other. No cross-check outlet for the $7M beyond aggregators (Seedtable, StartupIntros agree on August 2022 and $7M). Competitors empty: TechCrunch 2022 only mentions defunct Munchery and Sprig, undated for batch; no dated source found. Downgraded to depth 1 by orchestrator: the researcher reported combining the outcome and branding searches.
